title: session-calibration-sheet-haley
content:
Quick session sheet for small calibration sweeps — lean notes + table. Purpose: find a low-latency, low-cost config for the 7B quantized variant when doing short-turn chat (<=128 tokens).

Run summary (top-level):
- Date range: 2025-11-02 -> 2026-02-15 (iterative)
- Primary objective: p50 < 40ms and cost < $0.60 / 1k tokens for interactive loads when batching <= 8 and seq_len <= 128.
- Secondary: check KV-cache warmup impact and intermittent p95 spikes.

ASCII table of key runs (most recent top):
| run | date       | model        | quant   | batch | seq | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k | kv_warm | notes                          |
|-----|------------|--------------|---------|-------|-----|--------|--------|-------------|---------|--------------------------------|
| R042| 2026-02-15 | rw-7b-q4f    | q4f     | 4     | 64  | 36     | 110    | $0.52       | warm    | p95 spike during cold start    |
| R039| 2026-01-28 | rw-7b-q4f    | q4f     | 8     | 128 | 45     | 220    | $0.48       | cold    | batching 8 increases p95 a lot |
| R031| 2025-12-10 | rw-7b-q8     | q8      | 4     | 64  | 48     | 135    | $0.31       | warm    | cheaper but higher p50         |
| R025| 2025-11-16 | rw-7b-int8   | int8    | 2     | 32  | 28     | 90     | $0.67       | warm    | excellent p50, cost high       |
| R019| 2025-11-02 | rw-7b-q4f    | q4f     | 1     | 16  | 18     | 70     | $0.95       | warm    | baseline micro-latency         |

Interpretation notes:
- q4f gives best p50 at moderate cost; p95 sensitivity driven by batch size and cold starts.
- int8 runs give best raw latency but cost profile is worse due to licensing/ops (see linked PR).
- For interactive UX target (p50<40ms) we can ship q4f with batch=4 and aggressive KV caching. Need to mitigate p95 spikes for SLO.

Quick hypotheses to test (next sessions):
1) Reduce model kv cache eviction frequency (increase cache TTL) to see if p95 during short bursts drops.
2) Try hybrid strategy: route high-QPS flows to rw-7b-q4f batch=8 but with fallback to batch=4 when queue latency > 10ms.
3) Add lightweight local prefix cache (client) to avoid cold-start token generation for repeated prompts.

Commands / reproducible notes:
- Repro script (minimal):
  export MODEL=rw-7b-q4f
  python run_microbench.py --model $MODEL --batch 4 --seq 64 --iters 200 --kv-cache warm
- run_microbench.py args: --warm-start (preload KV), --latency-window 5000 (ms), --seed 42

Open questions / TODOs: 
- [ ] Check infra ticket INF-874 for autoscaler cooldown settings that may be causing cold-start amplification (linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Talk to SRE about NIC-level packet coalescing affecting p95 on GPU nodes (Ravi).
- [ ] Add synthetic tail probe to Redwood Console to capture p99 during ramp events.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep this sheet lean — copy into shared drive only after I have a clear experiment that changes rollout policy.
- If R042 p95 persists, create a canary rollout that forces warm pools for 10% of traffic.

Mini timeline of actions taken:
- 2025-11-02: initial micro-run single-request baseline (R019).
- 2025-11-16: early int8 run (R025) — promising latency but cost tradeoffs flagged.
- 2025-12-10: q8 run (R031) to test cost tradeoffs.
- 2026-01-28: larger batch stress (R039) revealed p95 sensitivity.
- 2026-02-15: focused kv-warm run (R042) — still seeing intermittent spikes during node reclaim.

Quick links / references for next session:
- Canaries doc: confluence://space/infra/canary-strategy (copy notes into INF-874).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/668 (kv-cache TTL change).
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime — thread "kv warmup p95" (see linked_artifacts).

End of sheet. Short-term plan: run 2 more sessions with cache-ttl=+30s and autoscaler cooldown=+10s; capture p95 and cold-start counts. If p95 reduces by >35%, escalate to product for canary config change.

Signature: Haley M. (personal tracker)
